A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CompBench, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A-F, while v3 ends after the references and repeatedly refers to supplementary material that is not supplied. This limits comparison of detailed procedures and supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 editing-model configurations in Tables 2-4, dataset statistics, and qualitative experimental results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports evaluations of 16 editing-model configurations, including newly reported human and Qwen evaluations in Table 4, alongside dataset statistics.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains MOSE preprocessing, four task-specific construction pipelines, MLLM-human validation, and instruction decomposition into four dimensions. The shortened description does not establish an actual construction-method change; missing implementation documentation is assessed under D1.

E1.justification: CompBench retains over 3,000 MOSE-derived pairs and the same nine editing tasks. Table 1 expands scene-complexity analysis to ImgEdit, GEdit-Bench, Complex-Edit, RefEdit, KRIS-Bench, and ComplexBench-Edit, extending dataset-characterization coverage without demonstrating new editing-model test tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 retain the original 13 model configurations and add Bagel, FLUX.1 Kontext, and Qwen-Image-Edit throughout the evaluation. These additions substantially strengthen the comparison set and occupy leading positions across numerous metrics.

E3.justification: Action, location, and viewpoint evaluation changes from GPT-4o alone to GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and human annotators. Table 4 replaces the average across tasks with per-task averages across evaluators. The foreground/background metrics and two-turn evaluation remain; revised numerical results alone do not establish other protocol changes.

E4.justification: v1 provides a blending-operation comparison in Figure 8 and extensive model-output case studies in Figures 15-19. These are absent from supplied v3, which still refers to supplementary evaluation material. Whether those analyses were retained elsewhere, revised, or removed cannot be established; the new mechanism discussion alone does not establish new ablations.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix D explicitly reports one GPT-4o evaluation per image pair at temperature zero; this run-count disclosure is absent from supplied v3. Neither supplied PDF reports confidence intervals or significance tests. Adding different evaluators does not itself constitute uncertainty estimation or establish increased repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 add substantial results, with Bagel leading 18 of 37 metrics. Retained-model values also change: MGIE's implicit-reasoning PSNR changes from 24.432 to 22.144, and SEED-X's second-turn PSNR from 13.793 to 17.708. Retained GPT-4o action/location scores remain unchanged, whereas viewpoint scores change. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Neither supplied PDF develops theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The retained task definitions and empirical metric descriptions introduce no identifiable change in formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: a complex instruction-guided editing benchmark with five categories, nine tasks, over 3,000 pairs, collaborative curation, and four-dimensional instruction decomposition. Expanded comparisons and updated model rankings support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds planner-executor misalignment, potential mitigation through unified architectures, and geometric hallucination, motivating pixel-level grounding and 3D structural guidance. This substantially extends v1's MLLM-and-reasoning interpretation. v1's explicit pipeline-cost, scalability, and reproducibility limitations in Appendix F are not included in supplied v3.

D1.justification: Self-contained reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced. v1 specifies PowerPaint, blending parameters, model inference configurations, eight A6000 GPUs, evaluator prompts, and annotation staffing; v3 largely defers such details to unavailable supplementary material. v3 adds a project-page address, but the PDFs alone do not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against newer editors and benchmarks, including Bagel, FLUX.1 Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit, Complex-Edit, ComplexBench-Edit, KRIS-Bench, and RefEdit. The introduction also shifts its scene-complexity criticism from synthetic-image reliance toward simplified real-image benchmarks.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, construction description, evaluation explanation, and conclusion undergo broad rewriting and compression. Insights is reorganized into four named themes, and appendix references become references to separate supplementary material. The main section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. Tables expand, especially Table 4's evaluator-by-task structure; v1 Figure 4 becomes separate Figures 4 and 5 without changing its underlying statistics. The overall-performance plot is redrawn, and Figure 1 replaces its viewpoint example. The new overall plot contains unexplained duplicate model-name variants.

improvement.justification: Newer comparators and human/Qwen scoring substantially strengthen the empirical assessment beyond v1's GPT-only evaluation. However, supplied v3 lacks v1's detailed reproducibility material and case studies, revises many retained-model scores without explaining why, and introduces duplicate model labels in Figure 6(b). These benefits and reporting weaknesses, compounded by unavailable supplementary material, prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
